judgments.rationale: The proposed edit adds the action 'provide' and action_quote 'provide', accurately drawn from the duty in F006 governing foreseeable leave based on planned medical treatment introduced in F004. It preserves the exact terms, conditions, exceptions, and modal force of the source text and existing baseline.

The proposal modifies the summary to state 'even if the date of the treatment requires leave to begin in less than 30 days', which directly contradicts F006. F006 establishes an express exception ('except that if the date of the treatment requires leave to begin in less than 30 days, the employee shall provide such notice as is practicable') rather than requiring 30 days' notice regardless.
The proposal modifies the summary text from 'shall' to 'must', which is an unnecessary paraphrase duplicate of the draft summary that already faithfully tracks the statutory phrasing 'shall' in F006.

source_spans.quote: (2) Duties of employee In any case in which the necessity for leave under subparagraph (C) or (D) of subsection (a)(1) or under subsection (a)(3) is foreseeable based on planned medical treatment, the employee—

(B) shall provide the employer with not less than 30 days’ notice, before the date the leave is to begin, of the employee’s intention to take leave under such subparagraph, except that if the date of the treatment requires leave to begin in less than 30 days, the employee shall provide such notice as is practicable.
